page: Vultr voc-s-24c-192gb-5760s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 12 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a bundled 5760 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core performance scoring in the top 25% of tested servers. Geekbench multi-core, image processing, and text processing metrics also rank in the top 25%, alongside Passmark CPU physics and extended instructions tests. Uncached memory bandwidth is a notable strength, with large-block read-only and write operations both placing in the top 10% tier. Conversely, cached small-block memory bandwidth, Passmark database operations, and Redis SET operations perform in the average middle 50% range.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers high resource density, combining substantial memory capacity with a large local NVMe SSD storage allocation. This makes it suitable for memory-intensive workloads and database deployments that require high uncached memory throughput without the overhead of external storage. Appropriate workloads include large-scale text and image processing, multi-threaded software compilation, and memory-bound applications. It is also capable of handling moderate LLM inference tasks, achieving average-tier performance for small and medium models.
